known_reference_characteristics: Two structural facts about the raymarch reference attributed here rather than chased, per render/raymarch.hpp's own header comment: (1) the reference's OWN silhouette error is +0.022% against an exact analytic sphere (SphereAnalyticSilhouetteAgreesWithTheExactCircleWithinHalfAPercent, test_render_raymarch.cpp), opposite in sign to tessellation's measured -1.54% under-coverage on the same sphere -- together, well under 2% of any band pinned here. (2) A systematic horizon-band deficit on any world with an infinite ground primitive (all ten shipped worlds use exactly one 'prim: plane' ground, confirmed by the controller amendments' own grep): a near-horizontal ray toward the analytic ground converges too slowly for the fixed step budget to reach, so raymarch under-counts a narrow band of rows nearest the true horizon, one-sided (raymarch never over-counts). At this file's 160x120, that band is consistently ~1 screen row (160 px, 0.83% of the frame) for every 'default' bookmark except circuit-track/figure-eight (see 'investigated' below); the 'top_down' bookmark shows it as flat 0.0 for all ten worlds because looking straight down places no horizon in frame at all.
investigated: circuit-track and figure-eight's 'default' bookmarks (pitch_radians=0.5235987755982988, i.e. exactly 30 degrees) measured roughly DOUBLE every other world's 'default' deficit (0.0166667 = 320 px, vs 0.0083333 = 160 px elsewhere) -- the largest values in the whole matrix, so this was checked rather than assumed benign. Cause, confirmed by the camera geometry itself, not merely plausible: with the default 60-degree vertical FOV (half-FOV 30 degrees), a camera pitched down by exactly 30 degrees points its TOP FRAME ROW exactly 30-30=0 degrees below horizontal -- precisely the mathematical horizon, the single worst case for the near-horizontal convergence limitation raymarch.hpp documents. Every other shipped world's 'default' bookmark is pitched at 25 degrees (0.4363323129985824 rad), leaving a comfortable 5-degree margin (top row sits at 25-30=-5 degrees, i.e. 5 degrees ABOVE horizontal, genuine sky) between the frame edge and the worst-case ray. This is the SAME already-diagnosed, already-attributed mechanism raymarch.hpp's header comment describes (not a second, undiagnosed defect) manifesting more strongly for this one camera framing because of where its pitch happens to sit relative to half-FOV; it is not a heightfield-ground gap (none of the ten shipped worlds has one, per the controller amendments' own grep) and it is more than 3x below the task's own >5% real-geometry-bug gate. Not chased, not fixed, not silently absorbed into a shared band -- named here, and both worlds' bands (0.025) are set from THEIR OWN measured maximum by the same uniform rule every other world uses, not widened further to hide the fact that they sit apart from the rest of the matrix.
